description: Compare each channel's average fee rate to the overall average fee rate across all linked fee records.

b.request: Among fee records linked to orders (`fees.orderslink` = `orders.recordvault`, with NULL `feerate` excluded), return one row for the `orders.orderbase` channels whose mean `feerate` exceeds the overall mean `feerate` across all those linked records, giving the mean of those channels' mean rates and the average amount by which they exceed the overall mean, unrounded
b.sql: WITH linked AS (SELECT o.orderbase, f.feerate FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate IS NOT NULL), overall AS (SELECT AVG(feerate) AS overall_mean FROM linked), channel AS (SELECT orderbase, AVG(feerate) AS channel_mean FROM linked WHERE orderbase IS NOT NULL GROUP BY orderbase), above AS (SELECT c.channel_mean FROM channel c CROSS JOIN overall ov WHERE c.channel_mean > ov.overall_mean) SELECT AVG(a.channel_mean) AS mean_of_channel_means, AVG(a.channel_mean - ov.overall_mean) AS avg_excess_over_overall_mean FROM above a CROSS JOIN overall ov;

a.request: Looking at fees linked to orders (`fees.orderslink` = `orders.recordvault`), compute each order channel's (`orders.orderbase`) average fee rate (`feerate`, ignoring missing values), and use the average fee rate over all those linked fee records as the benchmark. For the channels whose average is strictly above that benchmark, return a single row with the mean of their average fee rates and the mean of how far each one exceeds the benchmark, unrounded.
a.sql: WITH linked AS (SELECT o.orderbase, f.feerate FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate IS NOT NULL), channel AS (SELECT orderbase, AVG(feerate) AS chan_avg FROM linked GROUP BY orderbase), bench AS (SELECT AVG(feerate) AS benchmark FROM linked) SELECT AVG(c.chan_avg) AS mean_channel_avg, AVG(c.chan_avg - b.benchmark) AS mean_excess FROM channel c CROSS JOIN bench b WHERE c.chan_avg > b.benchmark;

c.request: For fees tied to orders (`fees.orderslink` = `orders.recordvault`), which order channels (`orders.orderbase`) have an above-average fee rate (`feerate`, ignoring missing values)? Give me one row: those channels' mean average fee rate and, on average, how far above average they are, unrounded. Compare each channel's average fee rate to the overall average fee rate across all linked fee records.
c.sql:
WITH linked AS (
  SELECT o.orderbase, f.feerate
  FROM fees f
  JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
  WHERE f.feerate IS NOT NULL AND o.orderbase IS NOT NULL
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(feerate) AS overall_avg FROM linked
),
chan AS (
  SELECT orderbase, AVG(feerate) AS chan_avg FROM linked GROUP BY orderbase
),
above AS (
  SELECT c.chan_avg, c.chan_avg - o.overall_avg AS gap
  FROM chan c CROSS JOIN overall o
  WHERE c.chan_avg > o.overall_avg
)
SELECT AVG(chan_avg) AS mean_above_avg_fee_rate,
       AVG(gap) AS avg_gap_above_overall
FROM above;

d.request: Compare each channel's average fee rate against the overall average fee rate across all fee records linked to orders (`fees.orderslink` = `orders.recordvault`), ignoring missing `feerate` values.
d.sql: WITH channel_fees AS (SELECT o.orderbase AS channel, AVG(f.feerate) AS channel_avg_fee_rate, COUNT(f.feerate) AS fee_count FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate IS NOT NULL GROUP BY o.orderbase), overall AS (SELECT AVG(f.feerate) AS overall_avg_fee_rate FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate IS NOT NULL) SELECT c.channel, c.channel_avg_fee_rate, c.fee_count, o.overall_avg_fee_rate, c.channel_avg_fee_rate - o.overall_avg_fee_rate AS diff_from_overall FROM channel_fees c CROSS JOIN overall o ORDER BY c.channel;
